title: A fence closes at any run of three backticks, whatever its opening length
body:
`closes_fence` in `lib.rs` ends a code block at any line made of three or more backticks:

```rust
fn closes_fence(line: &str) -> bool {
    let t = line.trim();
    t.starts_with("```") && t.trim_start_matches('`').is_empty()
}
```

CommonMark closes a fence only with at least as many backticks as opened it. So a block opened with four backticks, which holds a three-backtick fence as text, ends at that inner fence. The rest of the block is parsed as markdown, and the real closing fence opens a new, empty block. A markdown sample that contains code, the usual reason to open with four backticks, draws broken.

## Proposal

`fence` returns the opening's backtick count with the language, and the block closes only at a line of at least that many backticks and nothing else.

## Out of scope

- Fences opened with `~~~`, which cmr does not parse.
